prompt:
A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world each placement lands at the left-right mirror of the chosen anchor: a brick dx cells wide chosen at column x lands at column 8 - dx - x, in the same row. The valid-action mask is in the agent's own action terms. The designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
The starting network falls into the DONE-at-step-0 local optimum: by 25% of training it already stops placing bricks. The untrained trace shows why placements look bad. Actions are mirrored along x relative to the observation. An action at column x fills columns X-dx-x .. X-1-x (for example, 1x1 at col 2 fills col 5, and 1x2 at col 6 fills cols 0-1). Rows match. A convolutional head that ranks the anchor at (y,x) using features at (y,x) is therefore looking at the wrong cells. Every placement then scores near-random negative reward, and DONE (reward 0) wins. Correcting the action-to-cell mapping should be the change that matters most. I test: (1) a fixed x-flip of the features before the placement head; (2) the same flip with a recipe that gives more samples and more exploration; (3) a learned remap along each axis with no hard-coded flip, to see whether the network can find an unknown action layout itself, which matters for other worlds.

### Round 2
In this world the actions are mirrored along x, so the action for column x fills column X-1-x. Flipping the feature map before the footprint head fixes this: the starting architecture scored 0.00 and the plain flip scored 0.75. A learned axis remap (r1c3) never escaped the early collapse onto DONE. Dropping to 2 PPO epochs with ent_coef 0.02 gave 1.87x more samples and raised the score to 0.93. The two seeds of each trial are within about 5 points of each other, so the gap between 0.75 and 0.93 is larger than the noise and looks real. Training success was still rising at the end (0.80 at 75%, 0.84 at 100%), dev IoU is 0.989, and few cells land outside the target. So the remaining failures are probably about order or overhangs, or simply too few samples, not about perception. Training takes about 67 seconds, far under the 900-second limit. Next I test 1 PPO epoch (more samples), a longer reward horizon so the exact-build bonus counts for more, and a deeper trunk.

### Round 3
The x-flip before the footprint head is the key fix. It is exactly right: the traces show anchor x filling columns X-dx-x to X-1-x. A learned remap (r1c3) failed completely. The default network with 2 PPO epochs (r1c2, 0.93) and with 1 epoch (r2c1, 0.92) score the same within noise, so more samples alone has stopped helping. r2c1's training success levelled off at about 0.87. gamma 0.99 (0.87) and a deeper trunk at 1.38x compute (0.82, fewer samples, slower learning) were both worse. Dev IoU is about 0.99, so failures are near misses, probably order or overhang mistakes or a single wrong brick. Next I test the recipe's optimisation side (more updates per sample, a higher learning rate) on the same samples. I also test shifting compute from the stem and first conv into the footprint head, which must judge the landing layer non-linearly, without changing total compute.

### Round 4
Rounds 1–3 found one big fix: actions are mirrored along x relative to the observation, and flipping the features before the footprint head fixes it (0 → 0.75). Every gain after that came from the recipe. Cutting ppo_epochs from 4 to 2 gave 0.93; 1 epoch gave 0.92. Halving n_envs to 128 so there are twice as many updates gave the best score, 0.949 (r3c1), and the fastest early learning (0.29 training success at 25% of training, against 0.00 before). Changes that did not help or made things worse: lr 2e-3 (0.933, within noise), gamma 0.99 (0.87), a deeper trunk (0.82), moving compute into the head (0.86) and a learned axis remap (0). Seed spread is about 2–5 points. The evidence says this budget is limited by how many updates training gets, not by the network's capacity. For this last round I keep r3c1's network and push the update-frequency lever further: smaller batches, 1 epoch with more samples, and lower entropy now that early learning is fast.

## Trial it ended with
name: flip, half batches, ent 0.01
hypothesis: Same as r3c1 but ent_coef 0.01. The higher entropy was added to stop an early collapse onto DONE, but with n_envs 128 the agent already learns quickly (0.29 training success at 25%). A lower entropy bonus should let the policy sharpen, so greedy and training behaviour match more closely and exact builds are more reliable. Refuted if dev success falls below about 0.92 or a seed collapses to DONE.

Return a JSON object: "verdict" ("yes", "partly" or "no") and "evidence" (at most 80 words, quoting the text and
naming the round it comes from).
